issues.body: `sparq_gpu_is_still_unpublished` accepts any comment-stripped line whose trimmed text starts with `publish` and contains `false`; it does not verify the Cargo package `publish` field. For example, removing `publish = false` and adding the valid-but-unused manifest key `publish-note = false` makes this test pass while Cargo falls back to the default publishable state. A manifest containing `publish = true` plus such a line also passes. This contradicts the new lib.rs and threat-model claim that publication is an enforced trigger, leaving the security-model deferral capable of silently rotting.
issues.fix_hint: Inspect the crate's parsed Cargo metadata rather than manifest substrings. Cargo metadata exposes `packages[].publish`; select the `sparq-gpu` package and require that field to be an empty array (Cargo's representation of `publish = false`). Add a regression fixture or helper-level test proving that an absent/true publication setting plus an unrelated `publish-... = false` key is rejected.
issues.title: Publication tripwire can be bypassed by an unrelated manifest key

verdict.summary: Round 2's dependency-detection defect is fixed: Cargo metadata now enumerates actual workspace members and resolved dependency identities, with a real fixture covering quoted keys, renames, target/dev/build dependencies, and a member outside crates/*. However, the companion publication tripwire remains a textual heuristic and can report the crate as unpublished when Cargo considers it publishable. Because this is a new major finding even though the prior finding was resolved, progress is regressing.
